title: DNS cache persistence
banner: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Compare fresh/cached DNS answers; identify why immediate convergence cannot be assumed.
preconditions: JavaScript and standalone local HTML file access; no account or server
Fixed documentation-range addresses and display-only service.training.invalid
Synthetic switch at t=30, cached A expiry t=120, cached B expiry t=180
Declared retained-old overlap through t=180; three fixed journeys per comparison
10 synthetic ms budget; at most 12 measured comparisons
syntheticInput: Allowlisted retention, sample time, coverage, outcome and explanation choices; no user-supplied names, addresses, endpoints or DNS operations.
expectedAssertions: At t=30 fresh is new while both cached samples are old; retained destinations keep all three journeys usable
At t=120 cached B remains old even though cached A has expired
At t=180 agreement among three samples is not universal DNS convergence
Immediate old-destination retirement visibly interrupts cached journeys
Missing observations remain unknown with no invented answers or routing
Learner interpretation cannot rewrite measured outcomes, history or denominators
Strict typed input/state/phase/token guards, bounded history, native reset, keyboard/error UX and actual CSP enforcement work
limits: Every DNS/resolver/cache/routing/latency observation is fixed teaching DATA ONLY
No DNS queries or changes, host files, resolver/system settings, resources or real endpoints
One comparison per rehearsal and at most 12 comparisons; run-token limit 65535
Reset retains history; deliberate reload clears memory; no storage or persistence
No native proof, completed source parent, universal resolver behavior, production Node.js 24 validation or reliability certification
